digest.component_or_area: completion verifier banking and evidence framework
propositions: At search exhaustion, completion verifier banks met=false as evidence-of-absence (refutation) rather than absence-of-evidence, producing false FAIL verdicts on criteria whose evidence exists but was not reached within the search window

The banking layer conflates three distinct outcomes (met, refuted, insufficient) into a two-valued bool contract, preventing downstream consumers from distinguishing exhaustion from genuine refutation

Bounded fallback records carry no marker to indicate search-budget exhaustion versus positive evidence of absence, leaving remediation and close-gate refusal unable to distinguish and remediate appropriately

Consensus outcomes across the framework (schema, validation, rendering, sidecar, audit consumers) must carry the optional evidence_sufficient:false marker alongside met=false to preserve marker through all transformations and keep fail-closed gates unchanged

Model-facing tool must remain bool-only while the framework-level fallback path introduces a new record_insufficient() write contract to own marker generation, preventing models from emitting spurious sufficiency signals
